ops.new_text: \paragraph{Reader map.} The prospective dependency chain is typed as follows. An \emph{input row} is a serialized projective matrix with subgroup and loxodromic-eligibility evidence. Gate~Q may turn eligible rows into oriented primitive classes only after complete root and conjugacy decisions; quotienting those classes by inversion would then define the unoriented \emph{owners}. Gate~M may consume only such owners together with one immutable candidate-mechanism registry and may emit either a validated literal ideal or a typed stop receipt. A \emph{performance ledger} and its estimand may be constructed only from a reconciled Gate-Q population and a Gate-M-admissible registry. A missing or failed node prohibits every downstream use, and every node named here remains prospective.

The literal codomain is a deliberately strict frozen frame, not a canonical or literature-forced target. For a registered candidate \(M\) on eligible representatives, Gate~M requires the exact laws \(M(h\gamma h^{-1})=M(\gamma)\) for the frozen subgroup relation and \(M(\gamma^{-1})=M(\gamma)\) for descent to an unoriented owner. Gaussian conjugation \(\mathfrak p\mapsto\overline{\mathfrak p}\) is a separate codomain involution. Thus a candidate that instead yields \(M(\gamma^{-1})=\overline{M(\gamma)}\) fails unoriented descent when the two split prime ideals are distinct. Such a failure refutes only that registered candidate under the literal single-ideal codomain; it does not rule out other mechanisms or broader codomains.

The executed evidence synthesis was bounded to 48 record manifestations. Deduplication removed 12 duplicate manifestations; 36 unique records were screened at title or abstract level, 22 were admitted after scope screening, and 17 admitted records entered the workflow's peer-reviewed journal-or-correction numerator. The frozen inventory names P29-S01 through P29-S22, and independent verification records 22 \texttt{VERIFIED} existence outcomes with bounded metadata normalization. The accompanying evidence files preserve the queried interfaces, run dates, exact query strings, normalization rules, deduplication rule, admitted identifiers, and source-role coding. They do not preserve row-level identifiers and decisions for every screened-out manifestation, so the aggregate counts are auditable but a complete external-search replay is unavailable.

Each admitted record was encoded in a source-effect matrix with support class, claim-fitness grade, admissible use, prohibited stronger use, compatibility role, and locator limitation. The matrix was synthesized into the research report and then independently assessed from editorial, domain, methodology, and adversarial perspectives before author adjudication. This reader-facing account concerns evidence selection and synthesis only. It retrieved or created no new database record, publisher page, full text, passage, quotation, scientific artifact, experiment, or result.

Gate~M is a prospective logical and serialization contract. Before any collision outcome is visible, one candidate mechanism must be frozen by immutable formula bytes, source trace, admissible domain, literal-ideal codomain, normalization, associate convention, and the equations \(M(h\gamma h^{-1})=M(\gamma)\) and \(M(\gamma^{-1})=M(\gamma)\) on the frozen owner relation. The validator must distinguish a nonzero Gaussian prime ideal from an element, generator, norm, rational prime, composite ideal, factorization list, residue, or unordered conjugate pair. It must also record whether Gaussian conjugation fixes or exchanges the output. A split branch must follow from the registered formula rather than from observed collisions, and failure is scoped to that exact formula.

Gate~M has an explicit precedence rule. If the candidate violates literal split-branch compatibility under inversion, the primary disposition is \texttt{SPLIT\_IDEAL\_CODOMAIN\_OBSTRUCTION} and the same receipt records \texttt{formal\_map\_refuted=true}. If that predicate passes but another declared formal law fails, the disposition is \texttt{FORMAL\_MAP\_REFUTED}. Only a candidate passing every declared law and output-type check may receive \texttt{MECHANISM\_ADMISSIBLE}. These outcomes concern the exact registered candidate under the frozen frame, never all possible mechanisms or codomains, and none has been produced here.

The first prospective node is \texttt{ObjectLedger/v1}. Each row must contain canonical projective-matrix bytes, lift and central-sign conventions, subgroup-membership evidence, an exact loxodromic-eligibility disposition, serializer version, and hashes of every dependency. Its validator accepts only schema-conforming rows with reproducible membership and eligibility witnesses; malformed input yields \texttt{OBJECT\_ROW\_MALFORMED}, and an ineligible row yields an explicit exclusion receipt. Positive, negative, malformed, and serialization-round-trip fixtures must carry predeclared expected dispositions. No such ledger or fixture has been executed.

The second prospective node is \texttt{QuotientLedger/v1}. It must bind each admitted object hash to maximal-root, subgroup-conjugacy, inversion, transitive-closure, and canonical-owner decisions. Positive relations require replayable witnesses; negative decisions require a complete terminating procedure for the exact frozen relation. The validator rejects missing root exponents, unverifiable conjugators, inconsistent inverse links, nontransitive class IDs, and population totals that do not reconcile inputs, exclusions, repetitions, oriented classes, and unoriented owners. Root, inverse, conjugate, nonconjugate, malformed-witness, and resource-limit fixtures must have frozen expected stop states. No quotient ledger or fixture has been executed.

The third prospective node is \texttt{MechanismRegistry/v1}. A record must bind immutable formula bytes, domain, codomain, source trace, normalization, associate convention, split-conjugate treatment, and the exact conjugacy, inversion, and repetition predicates. The validator separately checks literal prime-ideal type, representative independence, and every declared law, and it attaches any failure only to the record hash. Fixtures must include admissible inert outputs, split conjugate pairs, a deliberate inversion-law failure, a nonprime output, a malformed formula record, and a timeout or unavailable-dependency case, each with a predeclared typed disposition. No mechanism record or fixture has been executed.

The fourth prospective node is \path{PerformanceLedger/v1}. It may consume only the exact \path{QuotientLedger/v1} population hash and a \path{MECHANISM_ADMISSIBLE} registry hash. Its schema must freeze baseline collisions, holdout membership, controls, clock, and the definition of \(S_H(M)\) before output access. The validator rejects raw-row scores, incomplete quotients, mismatched mechanism bytes, post-result control changes, or unreconciled populations. Fixtures must include a valid empty-result skeleton, a population-hash mismatch, a mechanism-hash mismatch, and a post-freeze mutation, all without supplying scientific values. No performance ledger or fixture has been executed.

The prospective \texttt{IndependentReplayReceipt/v1} must enumerate every consumed content hash, validator version, fixture identifier, expected disposition, observed disposition, and first mismatch. The verifier may reuse parsers and public schemas but must not import producer-side canonicalization, relation-decision, formula-evaluation, or scoring routines; those transformations require independently implemented checks or direct witness verification. Replay must cover positive, negative, malformed, inversion, root, and resource-limit fixtures and must fail closed on an unrecognized proof type. Agreement would certify only the registered finite procedure. No verifier, fixture execution, or receipt exists in the present work.

\paragraph{Prospective control interpretation.} An owner-label permutation preserves the quotient and tests scoring sensitivity to label identity; failure diagnoses label dependence but cannot establish arithmetic specificity. An inversion-paired control preserves the underlying owner population while testing representative independence; failure diagnoses an owner-law or serialization defect but cannot identify the correct ideal branch. A broadened-codomain control, such as an unordered conjugate pair, changes the output type and may diagnose whether a literal-branch obstruction is codomain-specific; it cannot rescue the registered single-ideal mechanism or count as performance under the frozen estimand. Every construction, statistic, and tolerance remains to be registered before output access, and no control has been run.

A later scientific implementation would expose five closed interfaces: \path{ObjectLedger/v1}, \path{QuotientLedger/v1}, \path{MechanismRegistry/v1}, \path{PerformanceLedger/v1}, and \path{IndependentReplayReceipt/v1}. Each interface must publish canonical bytes, dependency hashes, an allowed proof-type registry, validator acceptance predicates, and typed stop states. Producer and verifier may share only schemas, parsers, and witness formats; the verifier may not reuse producer-side canonicalization, relation-decision, mechanism-evaluation, or scoring logic. The required positive, negative, malformed, inversion, root, and resource-limit fixtures are specifications with expected dispositions, not executed tests. Accordingly, no replay, robustness, sensitivity, or usefulness result is reported.

The bounded contribution is a project-specific synthesis of typed owner semantics, a literal-ideal stress test, fail-closed Gate-Q and Gate-M contracts, and an independent-replay specification. Certificate methods, proof-carrying computation, and replay-oriented workflow design are therefore comparison classes rather than components claimed as new in isolation. The frozen source study did not perform a field-general novelty or priority review, so no global originality claim is made. Because the prospective schemas, fixtures, controls, and performance ledger have not been executed, practical usefulness and scientific performance also remain unevaluated.

The source study is bounded rather than exhaustive. The frozen files disclose queried interfaces, run dates, exact query strings, normalization and deduplication rules, admitted identifiers, and source-role decisions. They do not contain row-level identifiers and inclusion or exclusion decisions for every screened-out manifestation or a complete external-interface run log. The admitted 22-source corpus and aggregate counts can therefore be inspected, but the original search cannot be independently replayed record by record. This limitation precludes literature-absence, exhaustive-coverage, and novelty claims.

No separately authorized field-wide novelty analysis or passage adjudication was performed. The contribution is therefore limited to the manuscript's project-specific synthesis and prospective specification; it is not a priority claim against all certificate-methods, proof-carrying computation, or arithmetic-dynamics workflows. Source-role premises remain \texttt{INCONCLUSIVE} at passage level wherever no exact locator has been supplied, and the machine-audit comments preserve that boundary.
